source_text:
Homilia in festo palmarum
Τοῦ ἐν ἁγίοις Πατρὸς ἡμῶν Ἐπιφανίου ἐπισκόπου Κύπρου εἰς τὰ Βαΐα.
Κύριε, εὐλόγησον.
Χαῖρε σφόδρα, θύγατερ Σιὼν, τέρπου καὶ ἀγάλλου καὶ εὐφραίνου, πᾶσα ἡ
Ἐκκλησία τοῦ Θεοῦ· ἰδοὺ γὰρ πάλιν ὁ Βασιλεὺς πρὸς σὲ παραγίνεται. Ἰδοὺ ὁ σὸς
νυμφίος ἐπὶ πώλου ὡς ἐπὶ θρόνου καθήμενος ἔρχεται. Ἐξέλθωμεν εἰς ἀπάντησιν
αὐτοῦ, σπεύσωμεν ἰδέσθαι τὴν δόξαν αὐτοῦ, προφθάσωμεν φαιδρῶς εἰς τιμὴν τῆς
εἰσόδου αὐτοῦ. Πάλιν τῷ κόσμῳ σωτηρία, πάλιν ὁ Θεὸς ἐπὶ σταυρὸν ἔρχεται. Πάλιν ὁ
βασιλεὺς Σιὼν, τῶν ἐθνῶν ἡ προσδοκία ἐπὶ τὴν Σιὼν ἔρχεται, πάλιν τῷ κόσμῳ
σωτηρίαν χαρίζεται, πάλιν τὸ φῶς ἐφίσταται, πάλιν ἡ πλάνη πέπαυται, πάλιν ἀνθεῖ
ἡ ἀλήθεια, πάλιν ἡ Ἐκκλησία χορεύει, πάλιν ἡ Συναγωγὴ χηρεύει, πάλιν
αἰσχύνονται δαίμονες, πάλιν κατάρα λύεται, πάλιν Ἑβραῖοι ταράττονται, πάλιν ὁ
δράκων συντρίβεται, πάλιν τὰ ἔθνη εὐφραίνονται, πάλιν Σιὼν καλλωπίζεται.
Χριστὸς ἐπὶ πώλου ὡς ἐπὶ θρόνου καθήμενος ἔρχεται· οἱ οὐρανοὶ, ἀγάλλεσθε·
ἄγγελοι, ὑμνήσατε· τὰ ὄρη, εὐφραίνεσθε· οἱ βουνοὶ, σκιρτήσατε· ποταμοὶ, κροτήσατε·
οἱ ἐν Σιὼν, χορεύσατε· αἱ Ἐκκλησίαι, χαίρετε· ἱερεῖς, ὑμνήσατε· προφῆται,
προφθάσατε· μαθηταὶ, κηρύξατε· λαοὶ, ἀπαντήσατε· πρεσβῦται, συνδράμετε· αἱ
μητέρες, χορεύσατε· οἱ θηλάζοντες, ᾄσατε· νεανίσκοι, βοήσατε· τὰ ἔθνη, συνάχθητε.
Πᾶσα κτίσις, πᾶσα φύσις, πᾶσα τάξις, πᾶσα πνοὴ, πᾶσα ἡ γῆ, πᾶσα ἀξία, πᾶσα ἡλικία,
πᾶσα ἐθναρχία, πᾶσα βασιλεία, βασιλικῶς τῷ Βασιλεῖ τῶν βασιλέων ἀπαντήσωμεν,
δεσποτικῶς τῷ ∆εσπότῃ τῶν δεσποτῶν προσκυνήσωμεν, τῷ Θεῷ τῶν θεῶν θεϊκῶς
ἀναμέλψωμεν, τῷ 43.429 νυμφίῳ τῆς ἀφθαρσίας θεονύμφως χορεύσωμεν· τὰς
λαμπάδας φαιδροὶ φαιδρῶς ἐφαψώμεθα· τοὺς χιτῶνας τῶν ψυχῶν θεοπρεπῶς
ἐξαλλάξωμεν, τὰς τοῦ βίου ὁδοὺς καλῶς ἑτοιμάσωμεν, τὰς εἰσόδους τῶν ψυχῶν τῷ
Βασιλεῖ διανοίξωμεν, τὰ βαΐα τῆς νίκης ὡς νικητῇ τοῦ θανάτου βαστάσωμεν, τοὺς
κλάδους τῶν ἐλαιῶν τῷ ἐκ Μαρίας κλάδῳ θεοπρεπῶς ἐπισείοντες· τὰ ἀγγέλων τῷ
Θεῷ τῶν ἀγγέλων ὑμνήσωμεν· μετὰ τῶν παίδων θεοπρεπῶς ἀνακράξωμεν, μετὰ τοῦ
ὄχλου τὰ τοῦ ὄχλου καὶ οἱ ὄχλοι βοήσωμεν· Ὡσαννὰ ἐν τοῖς ὑψίστοις. Εὐλογημένος
ὁ ἐρχόμενος ἐν ὀνόματι Κυρίου· Θεὸς Κύριος, καὶ ἐπέφανεν ἡμῖν, ἐπέφανε τοῖς ἐν
σκότει καὶ σκιᾷ θανάτου καθημένοις ἡμῖν. Ἐπέφανεν ἡ τῶν πεπτωκότων ἀνάστασις,
ἐπέφανεν ἡ τῶν αἰχμαλώτων ἀνάῤῥυσις, ἐπέφανεν τῶν τυφλῶν ἡ ἀνάβλεψις,
ἐπέφανεν ἡ τῶν πενθούντων παράκλησις, ἐπέφανεν ἡ τῶν κοπιώντων ἀνάπαυσις,
ἐπέφανεν ἡ τῶν διψώντων ἀνάψυξις, ἐπέφανεν ἡ τῶν καταπονουμένων ἐκδίκησις,
ἐπέφανεν ἡ τῶν ἀπεγνωσμένων λύτρωσις, ἐπέφανεν ἡ τῶν ἀπεγνωσμένων
παράκλησις, ἐπέφανεν ἡ τῶν χωριζομένων ἕνωσις, ἐπεφάνη ἡ τῶν
καταπονουμένων ἐκδίκησις, ἐπεφάνη ἡ τῶν νοσούντων ἴασις, ἐπεφάνη ἡ τῶν
χειμαζομένων γαλήνη.
∆ιὸ καὶ ἡμεῖς, οἱ δῆμοι, μετὰ τοῦ ὄχλου βοήσωμεν, λέγοντες σήμερον Χριστῷ,
Ὡσαννὰ, τουτέστι, Σῶσον δὴ, ὁ ἐν ὑψίστοις Θεός. Ὢ καινῶν καὶ παραδόξων
πραγμάτων καὶ θαυμάτων! Χθὲς Χριστὸς ἐκ νεκρῶν ἤγειρε Λάζαρον, καὶ σήμερον ὁ
αὐτὸς ἐπὶ τὸν θάνατον ἔρχεται. Χθὲς ἄλλῳ, ὡς ζωὴ, ζωὴν ἐχαρίσατο, καὶ σήμερον
ζωοδότης ἐπὶ τὸν θάνατον ἔρχεται. Χθὲς Λαζάρου τὰ σπάργανα ἔλυσε, καὶ σήμερον ὁ
αὐτὸς ἐν σπαργάνοις δεσμευθῆναι ἑκὼν παραγίνεται. Χθὲς ἐν σκότοις ἐξήγαγεν
ἄνθρωπον, καὶ σήμερον ἐν σκοτεινοῖς τεθῆναι καὶ σκιᾷ θανάτου ἔρχεται διὰ τὸν
ἄνθρωπον. Χθὲς πρὸ ἒξ ἡμερῶν τοῦ Πάσχα διὰ τῶν πέντε αἰσθήσεων τὸν
τετραήμερον ὁ τριήμερος ταῖς δυσὶ τὸν ἕνα χαρίζεται ἀδελφὸν, καὶ σήμερον ἐπὶ τὸν
σταυρὸν ἔρχεται. Ἀλλὰ τῇ Μαρίᾳ μὲν τετραήμερον νεκρόν· τῇ δὲ Ἐκκλησίᾳ
τριήμερον ἑαυτὸν χαρίζεται ὁ Χριστός. Ἐκεῖ Βηθανία μόνη θαυμάζει, ἐνταῦθα δὲ
πᾶσα Ἐκκλησία ἑορτάζει.
thought_title: Rejoice, daughter Zion: the King comes on a colt
orientation: Epiphanius opens the Palm Sunday homily by calling the whole Church to rejoice because Christ the King and Bridegroom comes again to Zion on a colt.
pass_a_gloss: Rejoice greatly, daughter Zion, delight and exult and be glad, all the Church of God; for behold again the King comes to you. Behold your bridegroom seated on a colt as on a throne comes. Let us go out to meet him, let us hasten to see his glory, let us go before brightly in honor of his entry. Again salvation to the world, again God comes to the cross. Again the king of Zion, the expectation of the nations, comes to Zion, again he grants salvation to the world, again the light stands upon, again error has ceased, again truth blooms, again the Church dances, again the synagogue is widowed, again demons are put to shame, again the curse is loosed, again Hebrews are troubled, again the dragon is crushed, again the nations are gladdened, again Zion is adorned. Christ seated on a colt as on a throne comes; heavens, exult; angels, sing hymns; mountains, be glad; hills, leap; rivers, clap; those in Zion, dance; Churches, rejoice; priests, sing hymns; prophets, go before; disciples, preach; peoples, meet; elders, run together; mothers, dance; nursing infants, sing; young men, shout; nations, be gathered. All creation, all nature, all order, all breath, all the earth, all dignity, all age, all nation-rule, all kingdom, royally let us meet the King of kings, as servants let us worship the Lord of lords, to the God of gods divinely let us sing, to the bridegroom of incorruption in godly bridal manner let us dance; the lamps bright brightly let us kindle; the tunics of the souls in godly manner let us change, the roads of life well let us prepare, the entrances of the souls for the King let us open, the palm branches as to the victor over death let us carry, the branches of the olives to the branch from Mary in godly manner waving; the things of the angels to the God of angels let us sing; with the children in godly manner let us cry out, with the crowd the things of the crowd and the crowds let us shout: Hosanna in the highest. Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord; God the Lord, and he has appeared to us, he has appeared to us who sit in darkness and shadow of death. The resurrection of the fallen has appeared, the ransoming of the captives has appeared, the recovery of sight of the blind has appeared, the comfort of those who mourn has appeared, the rest of those who labor has appeared, the refreshment of those who thirst has appeared, the vindication of the oppressed has appeared, the redemption of the despairing has appeared, the comfort of the despairing has appeared, the union of those who are separated has appeared, the vindication of the oppressed has appeared, the healing of the sick has appeared, the calm of the storm-tossed has appeared. Therefore we too, the peoples, with the crowd let us shout, saying today to Christ, Hosanna, that is, Hosanna, O God in the highest. O new and paradoxical deeds and wonders! Yesterday Christ raised Lazarus from the dead, and today the same comes to death. Yesterday to another, as life, he granted life, and today the life-giver comes to death. Yesterday he loosed the grave-clothes of Lazarus, and today the same willingly comes to be bound in swaddling clothes. Yesterday he brought a man out of darkness, and today he comes to be placed in dark places and shadow of death for the man. Yesterday six days before the Passover through the five senses the three-day one to the two grants the one brother, the four-day one, and today he comes to the cross. But to Mary a four-day corpse; to the Church a three-day self Christ grants. There Bethany alone marvels, here the whole Church keeps feast.

choices.why: Glossary requires 'palm branches' for βαΐα; the genitive τῆς νίκης is kept as 'of victory' to preserve the source's explicit note that the branches signify victory.
Glossary requires 'Hosanna' as the rendering of the acclamation, not a translation.
This is the author's own explanatory gloss of Ὡσαννὰ, not the acclamation itself; rendering it as 'Save now' preserves the explanatory force of τουτέστι.
Glossary requires 'daughter Zion' as the fixed rendering.

pass_b_english: Rejoice greatly, daughter Zion; be glad, exult, and celebrate, all you Church of God. For look, the King is coming to you again. Look, your bridegroom is coming, seated on a colt as on a throne. Let us go out to meet him; let us hurry to see his glory; let us run ahead joyfully to honor his entry. Salvation comes to the world again; God comes to the cross again. The King of Zion, the hope of the nations, comes to Zion again. He grants salvation to the world again; the light rises again; error has ceased again; truth blooms again; the Church dances again; the synagogue is left widowed again; demons are put to shame again; the curse is broken again; the Hebrews are thrown into confusion again; the dragon is crushed again; the nations rejoice again; Zion is adorned again.

Christ is coming, seated on a colt as on a throne. Heavens, rejoice; angels, sing hymns; mountains, be glad; hills, leap; rivers, clap your hands; you who are in Zion, dance; churches, be joyful; priests, sing hymns; prophets, run ahead; disciples, proclaim; peoples, come to meet him; elders, run together; mothers, dance; nursing infants, sing; young men, shout; nations, gather together. Every creature, every nature, every order, every breath, all the earth, every rank, every age, every people, every kingdom—let us meet the King of kings in a manner worthy of a king; let us worship the Lord of lords in a manner worthy of a lord; let us sing to the God of gods in a manner worthy of God; let us dance for the bridegroom of incorruption as befits a divine bridegroom. Let us joyfully kindle our bright lamps; let us change the garments of our souls in a way worthy of God; let us prepare the roads of life well; let us open the entrances of our souls to the King; let us carry palm branches as for the victor over death, waving the olive branches in a way worthy of God before the branch from Mary. Let us sing the angels' hymn to the God of angels; let us cry out with the children in a way worthy of God; let us shout with the crowd what the crowds shout: "Hosanna in the highest. Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord" (Matthew 21:9; Psalm 117:26 (118:26)). God is the Lord, and he has appeared to us; he has appeared to us who sat in darkness and the shadow of death (Psalm 117:27 (118:27); Isaiah 9:2). The resurrection of the fallen has appeared; the deliverance of the captives has appeared; the recovery of sight for the blind has appeared; the comfort of those who mourn has appeared; the rest of the weary has appeared; the refreshment of the thirsty has appeared; the vindication of the oppressed has appeared; the redemption of the despairing has appeared; the consolation of the despairing has appeared; the union of those who were separated has appeared; the vindication of the oppressed has appeared; the healing of the sick has appeared; the calm for the storm-tossed has appeared.

Therefore let us also, the crowds, shout with the multitude, saying today to Christ: "Hosanna"—that is, "Save, we pray, O God in the highest." O what new and astonishing deeds and wonders! Yesterday Christ raised Lazarus from the dead, and today the same Christ goes to death. Yesterday, as life, he gave life to another, and today the giver of life goes to death. Yesterday he loosed Lazarus's grave cloths, and today the same one comes willingly to be bound in grave cloths. Yesterday he brought a man out of darkness, and today he goes to be placed in dark places and the shadow of death for the sake of humanity. Yesterday, six days before the Passover, the three-day one gave the one four-days-dead back to the two as a brother through the five senses, and today he goes to the cross. But to Mary he gave a brother four days dead; to the Church Christ gives himself, three days dead. There Bethany alone marvels, but here the whole Church keeps the feast.

problems.quote: Hosanna, O God in the highest
problems.source_quote: Σῶσον δὴ, ὁ ἐν ὑψίστοις Θεός
problems.why: Source gives Greek etymology 'Save now, O God in the highest', not 'Hosanna'.
problems.fix: Save now, O God in the highest

problems.quote: the one who is three days old gave the one four-days-dead brother back to his two sisters
problems.source_quote: ὁ τριήμερος ταῖς δυσὶ τὸν ἕνα χαρίζεται ἀδελφὸν
problems.why: τριήμερος here means 'the three-day one' (Christ risen after three days), not 'three days old'; the phrase is a typological parallel, not an infant.
problems.fix: the three-day one through the five senses gave the one four-days-dead back to the two as a brother
problems.ruling: τριήμερος means 'three-day one' (risen Christ), not 'three days old'; typological reference to resurrection is lost.

problems.quote: through the five senses the one who is three days old gave the one four-days-dead brother back to his two sisters
problems.source_quote: διὰ τῶν πέντε αἰσθήσεων ὁ τριήμερος ταῖς δυσὶ τὸν ἕνα χαρίζεται ἀδελφὸν
problems.why: The 'five senses' are not the means of raising Lazarus; the phrase likely refers to the five-day interval or the five senses being restored. The syntax is misread.
problems.fix: the three-day one gave the one four-days-dead back to the two as a brother through the five senses
problems.ruling: διὰ τῶν πέντε αἰσθήσεων is misread; likely refers to five-day interval or restored senses, not instrument of raising.

problems.source_quote: Εὐλογημένος ὁ ἐρχόμενος ἐν ὀνόματι Κυρίου
problems.why: LXX Psalm 117:26 (Hebrew 118:26); brief requires LXX numbering noted.
problems.ruling: LXX Psalm 117:26, not 118:26; if brief requires LXX numbering, this misleads readers on the reference.

problems.why: LXX Psalm 117:27 (Hebrew 118:27); brief requires LXX numbering noted.
problems.ruling: LXX Psalm 117:27, not 118:27; if brief requires LXX numbering, this misleads readers on the reference.

problems.why: English omits 'the vindication of the oppressed has appeared' (ἐκδίκησις), present twice in source.
problems.fix: the vindication of the oppressed has appeared; the healing of the sick has appeared; the calm for the storm-tossed has appeared
problems.ruling: Source has ἐπεφάνη ἡ τῶν καταπονουμένων ἐκδίκησις repeated; English omits second instance, losing meaning.

The second and third problems were real and related: the source's τριήμερος means 'the three-day one' (Christ risen after three days), not 'three days old', and the syntax was misread. The English was corrected to reflect the typological parallel.
